text:
QUESTIONS, aimed at the weakest links first. Each question decides between two build choices.

Q1: Does a 45-step smoke run reproduce the full run's learning-rate schedule at steps 30–45? | decides: `--smoke-steps 45` vs `--smoke-seconds` cutoff with the 1525-step schedule left in place
A1: No. With `--smoke-steps 45`, `lr_mult` gets warm = max(1, int(0.9)) = 1 and cool_start = int(31.5) = 31. So indices 31–44 decay linearly from 1.0 to 1/14, and the KILL window would be mostly annealed loss. In the full run, warm = 30 and cool_start = 1067, so steps 30–45 are the first full-LR steps. `--smoke-seconds` keeps total_steps = 1525 and only breaks on time, so its `loss_curve[:45]` matches the full run step for step. Use it, with a time budget that covers at least 45 steps, and read `loss_curve[29:45]`.

Q2: Do arms with the same seed see identical batches? | decides: paired same-seed differencing vs pooled unpaired Welch for the KILL rule
A2: Yes, provided the build keeps them identical. `Shards` draws from its own `np.random.default_rng(seed)`, which only `sample()` consumes, so batch k is the same in every arm with the same seed. Torch init is also identical as long as s and b are created with `torch.zeros`/`torch.full` (no RNG calls). The counted prior must be computed from a fixed slice, for example the first N tokens of `train_000`, never through `train.rng`. Under these conditions, batch-content noise cancels in the per-seed arm difference.

Q3: Is a same-seed rerun bitwise reproducible, so that the paired noise floor is zero? | decides: measure the floor with A/A same-seed reruns vs force `torch.use_deterministic_algorithms(True)` for the probe runs
A3: Unknown. The tied table receives an embedding-backward gradient and an SDPA backward gradient, and PyTorch lists several CUDA backward ops as nondeterministic (https://pytorch.org/docs/stable/notes/randomness.html). Under bf16 and Muon at full LR, any bit difference will grow. Two same-seed baseline reruns give the paired floor directly: the sd of their `mean(loss_curve[29:45])` difference.

Q4: What is the across-seed sd of the 15-step mean training loss? | decides: an unpaired 3+3 Welch kill vs a paired or longer-window kill
A4: Unknown here. It can be computed at no cost from the three existing baseline seeds' `loss_curve` (the layer-0 gradient measurement already used 3 seeds). My belief: 32 windows per step with a window-level loss sd of about 0.4–0.5 nats gives about 0.07–0.09 per step. Seed-dependent data then makes the 15-step mean sd about 0.015–0.025 nats, plus init variance.

Q5: What sd would let 3 seeds resolve a 0.005 margin? | decides: 3 seeds vs 5–8 seeds (or a paired design)
A5: Unpaired Welch with 3+3 and equal variance has df ≈ 4 and t₀.₉₉ = 3.747. SE = 0.816·s, so it needs s < 0.0016 nats, which is about 10× below my belief in A4. That is not resolvable. Paired with n = 3 (df 2, t₀.₉₉ = 6.965) needs sd_d < 0.00124. With n = 5 (t = 3.747) it needs sd_d < 0.0030; with n = 8 (t = 2.998), sd_d < 0.0047. Three seeds resolve 0.005 only if the A/A floor from A3 is about 0.001 or less.

Q6: Is the logged loss precise enough to see 0.005? | decides: use `loss.item()` as is vs log an explicit fp32 loss
A6: Probably yes. `log_softmax`/`nll_loss` are on autocast's float32 list (https://pytorch.org/docs/stable/amp.html), so the loss should be fp32, and `loss_curve` rounds to 1e-4. If it were bf16, the grid spacing in the 4–8 range would be 0.031. Print `loss.dtype` once to confirm.

Q7: Is steps 30–45 the right phase for the bias-only vs direction-only margin? | decides: KILL window 30–45 vs a later window (e.g. 200–300 at full LR)
A7: Probably not for L4. The baseline is already at 7.06 by step 26, which I believe is below the GPT-2-token unigram entropy of about 7.5 nats (unchecked). The unigram prior is therefore largely learned by step 30, and any bias advantage there is a transient. The representation effect that L4 claims would show later, and the A/A noise floor also grows with step count. Both windows need the A3 measurement.

Q8: Does the bias gradient change grad clipping, confounding the comparison against the baseline? | decides: clip over all params vs exclude s and b from `clip_grad_norm_`
A8: Possibly. `clip_grad_norm_` covers every parameter, and b's gradient (mean softmax minus empirical frequency) has norm up to √2. Whenever the baseline's total norm is near 1, adding b scales down every other update. This is shared by bias-only and direction-only, but it confounds the comparison with the baseline. Log the value `clip_grad_norm_` returns in all arms.

Q9: Should the readout be the training-loss window or a fixed probe set? | decides: `loss_curve[29:45]` mean vs a fixed probe of train windows evaluated after step 45
A9: A fixed probe gives a paired, step-free readout plus per-band rare-token losses for L4 at no extra cost. Example: 64 windows from the tail of the last `train_*.bin`; the sampler's overlap with them is negligible, and val is never touched (C6). However, smoke runs save no `model.pt`, so the probe has to live in the script (train-only) or a separate tool needs a weights dump. Unknown which the harness tolerates.

Q10: Must the bias-only arm share the direction-only arm's bias init? | decides: zero-init bias-only vs counted-init bias-only as the comparison arm
A10: Yes. L1 predicts that counted vs zero init alone moves step-26 loss by 0.03–0.3. That is 6–60× the 0.005 margin, so mismatched inits make the KILL test measure init instead of normalization. Use counted init in both arms, or zero in both.

KNOWN:
- `--smoke-steps 45` gives warm = 1 and cool_start = 31; the full run gives warm = 30 and cool_start = 1067 out of 1525 steps. Steps 30–45 have different LR in the two modes. [script]
- `--smoke-seconds` keeps the 1525-step schedule, so `loss_curve[:45]` is schedule-identical to the full run. [script]
- `loss_curve[i]` is the pre-update loss of step i+1, averaged over 8 micro-batches × 4 × 1024 = 32,768 tokens. [script]
- `Shards` uses its own numpy rng seeded by `--seed`, independent of torch, so same seed means the same batches in every arm. [script]
- s and b must be initialised without torch RNG calls, and the counted prior must come from a fixed shard slice, not `train.rng`, or pairing breaks. [belief]
- Unpaired Welch with 3+3 seeds resolves 0.005 only if the per-arm sd is below 0.0016; paired with 3 seeds needs sd_d below 0.00124; paired with 5 needs below 0.0030. (t₀.₉₉: df2 = 6.965, df4 = 3.747, df7 = 2.998.) [belief]
- The same arithmetic applies to C7's exam test. With an exam sd of 0.004, 3+3 needs a true gain of about 0.017 nats, not 0.005. [belief]
- Losses go through `log_softmax`, which is on autocast's float32 list, so the logged loss is fp32 (https://pytorch.org/docs/stable/amp.html). [web]
- PyTorch documents several CUDA backward ops as nondeterministic, so same-seed reruns may diverge (https://pytorch.org/docs/stable/notes/randomness.html). [web]
- `clip_grad_norm_` (clip at 1.0) covers all parameters, including any new bias. [script]
- Scale-invariant weights trained with decay grow their norm through tangential steps until decay balances it (https://arxiv.org/abs/2006.08419). AdamW's per-coordinate normalisation also leaves a radial component, so L3's "norm set only by input and decay" is incomplete. [web]
- Three baseline seeds already exist with loss curves (from the layer-0 gradient measurement). Computing their across-seed sd of `mean(loss_curve[29:45])` is free. [measured]

ASSUMES:
- Training loss at early matched steps predicts the exam's final val loss.
- One seed controls data order and init together; nothing separates data noise from init noise.
- Training is deterministic enough that same-seed arms differ only by the mechanism.
- The KILL margin is a point estimate, not a significance test.
- The LR schedule seen in the probe run equals the full run's.
- The output prior belongs in the head, not in the residual stream or the input.
- All vocabulary rows share one table and one AdamW group with weight decay 0.1.

NEW IDEAS:

SLOT: drop
IDEA: Partial untie, 16 output-only dimensions
MECHANISM: Drop "all rows share one table". The head uses `cat(E[:, :368], U)` with U of size 50304×16 as an output-only parameter, while the input still reads all 384 dimensions of E. This gives a small private channel to the output side for frequency and anisotropy.
PREDICTION: Non-embedding parameters reach about 22.05M; loss beats bias-only at steps 200–300 as the output prior moves into U.
TEST: 300 schedule-matched steps (`--smoke-seconds`) on 3 paired seeds against bias-only.
SOURCE: own
PART: Inputs and outputs: tied embedding, stream read-out, logits
KIND: leap
BREAKS: Full tying of every dimension.
KILL: Paired mean of `loss_curve[199:300]` not below bias-only by at least 0.01 on all 3 seeds.

SLOT: strengthen
IDEA: Direction-only on both sides
MECHANISM: Also RMS-normalise the input lookup and multiply it by a separate per-token input scale. Row norm then carries no meaning anywhere, and the two roles get two independent scalar vectors.
PREDICTION: Spearman correlation between row norm and log frequency drops below 0.2 by step 100; layer-0 attention gradient falls toward layer-1 levels.
TEST: 100 paired steps; log the layer-0 grad norm and the norm/frequency Spearman correlation.
SOURCE: own
PART: Inputs and outputs: tied embedding, stream read-out, logits
KIND: port

SLOT: specialise
IDEA: Training-wheel counted prior, faded out by step 300
MECHANISM: A frozen counted log-unigram buffer is added to the logits with weight λ(t), going from 1 to 0 linearly over steps 0–300. The prior is used only in the phase where it helps, and the final model's forward is plain.
PREDICTION: A 1–3 nat gain at steps 1–10, and no loss jump as λ reaches 0 if the rows have absorbed the prior.
TEST: Compare paired `loss_curve` slopes around step 300 against baseline.
SOURCE: own
PART: Inputs and outputs: tied embedding, stream read-out, logits
KIND: leap
BREAKS: The logit function is fixed throughout training.
KILL: Loss at steps 300–350 more than 0.01 above paired baseline.

SLOT: port
IDEA: Per-token stream-entry weights
MECHANISM: Replace `expand(-1, -1, 4, -1)` with per-token 4-vector weights (50304×4, initialised to 1) so token identity chooses which Sinkhorn streams it enters, moving per-token salience out of row norm.
PREDICTION: Mid-frequency band (rank 100–10k) loss falls by at least 0.01 at step 300.
TEST: 300 paired steps with a band-wise probe.
SOURCE: own
PART: Residual streams: Sinkhorn mixing and read/write weights
KIND: port

SLOT: combine
IDEA: Direction-only head with lazy row decay
MECHANISM: Combine the direction-only head with LazyAdam-style sparse decay (https://www.tensorflow.org/addons/api_docs/python/tfa/optimizers/LazyAdam): decay is applied only to rows looked up in the current batch, so rare rows stop shrinking on every step while their output direction stays intact.
PREDICTION: Rank-10k+ band loss falls by at least 0.02 compared with direction-only.
TEST: 300 paired steps, band-wise probe.
SOURCE: https://www.tensorflow.org/addons/api_docs/python/tfa/optimizers/LazyAdam
PART: Inputs and outputs: tied embedding, stream read-out, logits
KIND: port

- Does the A/A floor grow by step 300 enough to make a later window worse than 30–45? | build: yes | decides: KILL window 30–45 vs 200–300

- Will the harness accept an in-script train-slice probe? | build: yes | decides: in-script probe vs `loss_curve` only
- What is the across-seed sd of the exam val loss at 1525 steps? | build: no | decides: (sets how many seeds the C7 claim needs)

LINK STATUS:
- L1: open | No counted-init run exists yet. If measured, it is resolvable even with 3 seeds, since the predicted gap of 0.03–0.3 is far above the noise.
- L2: open | Anisotropy is unmeasured in both arms.
- L3: open | The output gradient's radial component is exactly zero under row normalisation, but AdamW updates and tangential growth still change norms (https://arxiv.org/abs/2006.08419), so the predicted Spearman drop is not guaranteed.
- L4: open | The −0.005 threshold over 3 seeds is resolvable only if the paired sd_d is below 0.00124; unpaired it needs s below 0.0016, about 10× below my belief. The bias-only arm must also share the counted init (A10).
- L5: open | At an exam sd of about 0.004, a 0.005 exam gain is not provable with 3+3 seeds; a gain of about 0.017 or more is needed.
